title: Elijah Taken Up
summary: King Ahaziah falls through a lattice and sends to consult Baal-zebub; Elijah intercepts his messengers and calls down fire on two captains with fifty men each before sparing the third. As Elijah and Elisha cross the Jordan, Elijah is taken up in a whirlwind by a chariot and horses of fire, and Elisha takes his mantle and divides the Jordan with it. Elisha heals the waters of Jericho with salt, and youths who mock him at Beth-el are mauled by two she-bears.

title: Elisha and Moab
summary: Mesha of Moab rebels, and Jehoram of Israel, Jehoshaphat of Judah and the king of Edom march through the wilderness and run out of water. Elisha, for Jehoshaphat's sake, says the valley will fill with water without wind or rain and that Moab will be given into their hands. In the morning the water looks like blood to the Moabites, who think the kings have fought each other, and they are routed. The Moabite king offers his firstborn son on the wall, and great wrath falls on Israel.

title: The Widow's Oil and the Shunammite's Son
summary: Elisha helps a prophet's widow by multiplying a jar of oil so that she can pay her debt. A Shunammite woman builds him a room, and he promises her a son; when the boy later dies, Elisha lies on him and he revives. In a famine Elisha makes a poisonous stew harmless with meal, and with twenty barley loaves he feeds a hundred men, with some left over, as the LORD had said.

title: Naaman Healed
summary: Naaman, commander of the king of Syria's army, has leprosy, and a captive Israelite girl tells his wife of a prophet in Samaria. Elisha tells him by messenger to wash seven times in the Jordan; Naaman is furious but his servants persuade him, and he is healed. He says there is no God in all the earth but in Israel and refuses payment. Elisha's servant Gehazi follows Naaman for silver and clothing, lies to Elisha, and is struck with Naaman's leprosy.

title: Elisha and the Arameans
summary: At the Jordan, Elisha makes an axe head float. When Syria's king tries to capture him, Elisha prays that the army be struck blind, leads them to Samaria, and the king of Israel feeds them and sends them home. Later Ben-hadad besieges Samaria and the famine is so bad that two women plan to eat their sons. Elisha predicts cheap flour the next day; four lepers find the Syrian camp abandoned, the city is relieved, and the officer who doubted is trampled at the gate.

title: Jehu's Revolt
summary: After Hazael of Syria kills Ben-hadad, Elisha sends a young prophet to anoint Jehu as king, and Jehu rides to Jezreel and shoots Joram, king of Israel, and Ahaziah of Judah. Jezebel is thrown from a window and eaten by dogs, as Elijah had said. Jehu has Ahab's seventy sons killed and their heads piled at the gate, and kills Baal's worshipers in their temple. The LORD promises four generations of kings, but Jehu does not leave the golden calves.

title: Athaliah and Joash
summary: When Ahaziah of Judah dies, his mother Athaliah kills the royal family, but his sister Jehosheba hides the infant Joash in the temple for six years. In the seventh year the priest Jehoiada arranges with the captains to crown Joash, with guards around him. Athaliah cries 'Treason' and is put to death. Jehoiada makes a covenant, the Baal temple is destroyed, and Joash repairs the temple with funds from a chest by the altar, though he later pays tribute to Hazael.

title: Elisha's Death and the Wars of Jehoash
summary: The dying Elisha has King Jehoash strike the ground with arrows to signify victories over Syria. Elisha dies, and a dead man thrown into his tomb revives on touching his bones. Later Jehoash defeats Amaziah of Judah, breaks down part of Jerusalem's wall, and takes treasure from the temple; Amaziah is killed in a conspiracy. Jeroboam II restores Israel's borders, as the prophet Jonah had said.

title: The Fall of Samaria
summary: Kings follow one another in Israel and Judah, Israel's line marked by assassinations. Ahaz of Judah sends tribute to Tiglath-pileser of Assyria and copies an altar he sees in Damascus. Hoshea rebels against Assyria, and Shalmaneser besieges Samaria for three years. Israel is carried off to Assyria, and the text explains the exile as the result of idolatry despite the prophets' warnings. Settlers brought in from other lands carry their own gods and fear the LORD only partly.

title: Hezekiah and Sennacherib
summary: Hezekiah removes the high places, breaks the bronze serpent, and rebels against Assyria. Sennacherib takes Judah's fortified cities and is paid tribute, but the Rabshakeh still stands before Jerusalem and mocks trust in the LORD and Egypt. Hezekiah goes into the temple, spreads out Sennacherib's letter, and prays; Isaiah says the king will not enter the city. That night the angel of the LORD kills 185,000 in the Assyrian camp, and Sennacherib returns home and is killed by his sons.

title: Hezekiah's Illness and the Babylonian Envoys
summary: Hezekiah, mortally ill, is told by Isaiah to set his house in order; he prays and weeps, and God adds fifteen years and promises to deliver the city. Isaiah applies a lump of figs, and as a sign the shadow on the dial of Ahaz goes back ten degrees. Envoys from Merodach-baladan of Babylon visit, and Hezekiah shows them everything he has. Isaiah says it will all be carried to Babylon, and Hezekiah calls the word good, since there will be peace in his days.

title: Manasseh, Amon and Josiah
summary: Manasseh, king for 55 years, rebuilds the high places, serves Baal and the host of heaven, sets an idol in the temple, and sheds much innocent blood. His son Amon is killed after two years. Josiah, king at eight, has the high priest Hilkiah find the book of the law in the temple in his eighteenth year. Huldah the prophetess says judgment will still come; Josiah reads the book to the people, renews the covenant, removes idols, and keeps a great Passover. He is killed at Megiddo by Pharaoh Necho.

title: The Fall of Jerusalem
summary: Josiah's sons Jehoahaz, Jehoiakim and Zedekiah reign in turn under Egyptian and then Babylonian pressure. Nebuchadnezzar takes Jehoiachin and the nobles to Babylon; Zedekiah rebels, and the city is besieged for about two years. In his eleventh year the wall is broken, Zedekiah's sons are killed before him and he is blinded, and the temple and palace are burned and the people taken. Gedaliah, appointed governor, is assassinated, and Jehoiachin is later freed in Babylon.
